title: Frontend: React + Next.js
tagline: Full-stack web app for customers and owners
goal: Build the web app for customers and business owners on top of the Week 2 API.
outcomes: Build reusable React components and understand server vs client components
Manage forms and state immutably, sharing Zod schemas with the backend
Fetch server state with TanStack Query, handle races and 409 conflicts
Implement cookie-based auth, protected routes and role-based UI
Ship accessible, responsive UI (Lighthouse a11y 90+) with time-zone-correct dates
Test with React Testing Library and Playwright
projectStage: Booking Web App v1 — monorepo (api/, web/, packages/shared). Customer booking flow + owner dashboard on Next.js.

days.title: React + Next.js Basics
learn: Components, props, JSX, children, lists and keys
Vite vs Next.js and when each is used
npm workspaces
Next.js App Router, layouts, server vs client components, dynamic routes, 404 pages
tasks: Scaffold Next.js with TypeScript. Put api/ and web/ in one repo with npm workspaces and a packages/shared folder for the Zod schemas. Update the CI workflow paths in the same PR so CI stays green.
Build pages: /, /services, /services/[id], /book, /bookings/[id], /login, /signup, /dashboard.
Build reusable Header, Footer, Button and ServiceCard components.
Add a nav bar with active link highlighting.
Render the services list from the API on the server.
acceptance: Components are reusable, and lists use stable keys.
404 is handled, including an unknown id on a detail page.
Navigation is client-side (no full page reloads).
No inline styles and no direct DOM manipulation.
Can explain which components run on the server and which run in the browser.

days.title: State, Forms + Validation
learn: useState, controlled inputs, immutable state updates
React Hook Form
Sharing Zod schemas between frontend and backend
Conditional rendering, loading and disabled button states
tasks: Build the booking form: service, date, time slot, contact details.
Show validation errors next to each field.
Build the owner's service manager with useState: add and remove services in a list, show the count and an empty state.
acceptance: The same Zod schema validates on the client and the server.
Submit is disabled while the request is in flight.
The form is fully usable by keyboard.
State is updated immutably (no push or splice on state arrays).

days.title: Data Fetching + Server State
learn: fetch with credentials: "include" and CORS credentials for cookies
useEffect dependency arrays and cleanup, and why to avoid useEffect for fetching
An API service layer (one place for every fetch call)
TanStack Query (caching, refetching, mutations, optimistic updates), race conditions, handling 409 Conflict
tasks: Wire a bare login form that calls POST /login with credentials: "include", and allow credentials for http://localhost:3000 in the API's CORS config.
Fetch availability when the date changes.
Book a slot, then refresh availability.
Handle "slot just got taken" (409) with a clear message.
acceptance: Each date change fetches once (no loops, no stale results overwriting newer ones).
Loading, error and empty states for every fetch.
Two browser tabs booking the same slot: one succeeds, the other sees a clear message.

days.title: Auth on the Frontend
learn: Global state with Context API or Zustand
Cookie-based login from the browser, Google sign-in button
Protected routes with proxy.ts (middleware.ts before Next.js 16)
Role-based UI, logout
tasks: Connect login, signup and Google sign-in to the backend, and move the Google account-linking confirm form into Next.js.
Keep the logged-in user in global state (Context or Zustand).
Protect /dashboard: owners see all bookings, staff see their own schedule, customers see their history. Owners get a paginated, searchable bookings list (server-side).
Logout clears the session.
acceptance: Auth persists across routes and page refresh.
Invalid login shows a clear error message.
Logged-out users are redirected away from protected pages.
Hidden buttons are not the only protection (the backend still checks roles).

days.title: UX Polish, Accessibility + E2E Tests
learn: Responsive layouts, accessible components, time zones in the UI
React Testing Library, Playwright E2E tests
tasks: Owner dashboard actions: cancel and mark done from today's bookings. Add PATCH /bookings/:id/status (owner only) and a migration adding the 'completed' status.
Add tabs for Upcoming / Completed / Cancelled on the dashboard.
Store the business time zone (for example Asia/Kolkata) and show all times in it.
Playwright test for the full flow: sign up → book → see booking → cancel.
Ask the AI agent to write React Testing Library tests for the login form and to explain the auth state code. Review, correct and run them, and note where it was wrong.
acceptance: Works at 360px and 1440px.
With the laptop set to another time zone, a 10:00 booking still shows 10:00.
Keyboard navigable, Lighthouse accessibility score 90+.
E2E test runs green locally.

days.title: Debug Lab (no AI)
learn: React DevTools
The Network tab against a real backend
Reading hydration errors
brokenLab: A useEffect with an unstable dependency that refetches on every render (check with next build and next start, since Strict Mode runs effects twice in dev)
Index keys that make the wrong booking update on cancel
A hydration mismatch from a date rendered in the server's time zone
tasks: Fix all five issues in the provided booking frontend, with a test for each.
acceptance: All five fixed, with a test for each.
Tests cover login and the bookings list.
Each fix written up as: symptom → cause → fix → how verified.

days.title: Weekly Project: Booking Web App v1
tasks: Client message: "Customers want to book online instead of calling, and I need to see my day at a glance." Update the scope first.
Customer flow: browse services, pick a slot, book, see and cancel own bookings.
Owner dashboard: bookings by day, cancel, mark done, manage services.
Email/password + Google login, role-based pages.
Loading, error and empty states everywhere.
Unit tests + one Playwright E2E test (run locally this week; it moves into CI in Week 4).
acceptance: See the rubric on the Project tab.
